content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I resolved an issue with Hoppers in my project. The program runs correctly in simulation, but I have not been able to test it with the actual hardware yet. After transferring the project, I receive the message: 'Memory distribution exceeded' in the LSC message window. Will the program still run? Or should I rearrange the layout blocks and download it again from the controller to the PC? There are approximately 320 blocks, with program memory usage at 2700/8500. I am using [product_name] [version_no]. Thank you for your response.
Could you please share a screenshot of the message and show the details from the info window?

Pressing F2 usually generates a report: Note: Layout memory 34777/30000. This value exceeds the limit but it's generally not a serious issue. This memory stores the placement of program elements in [product_name]; if it is exceeded, uploading from the device will result in a program without an organized layout.
I only have access to the info window at the moment, so I can't provide the exact message.

As [user_name] mentioned, the layout memory is insufficient. However, this does not affect the execution of your program. It only means that if you reload from the device, the blocks may no longer be arranged as originally designed.
Thank you both for your help.
I noticed your program has a deep nesting structure. Please be aware that there is a limitation to this. For more information, search for 'nesting' in the software help. Cheers, [user_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Users discussed receiving a 'Memory distribution exceeded' message when working with a program on [product_name] [version_no] using [product_name] software. The main concern was whether this warning affects program execution. It was clarified that this message pertains only to memory used for visual layout, not for running the program. Therefore, the program will operate normally, but the arrangement of blocks could become disorganized if reloaded from the device.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the program to function as normal on the [product_name] [version_no] hardware and wishes for the program's visual block arrangement to remain organized when reloading or transferring the project.
